summary: The reader has finished an undergraduate computer science degree: asymptotic analysis, discrete mathematics (modular arithmetic, primes, binary representation, induction), introductory linear algebra (vectors, matrices, inverses, dot products), and the calculus the degree requires (limits, convergence of sequences and series, basic integrals). They know basic Turing machines with several tapes and standard algorithm analysis, including recurrences and schoolbook multiplication. They have not studied the FFT-based multiplication literature, abstract algebra beyond basics, or tape-level data-movement algorithms.

known.name: Binary representation and bit operations
known.gloss: Integers written in base 2, with bitwise operations such as XOR acting on their digits.

known.name: Modular arithmetic
known.gloss: Arithmetic on integers where values differing by a multiple of the modulus are identified.

known.name: Prime numbers and coprimality
known.gloss: Primes are integers greater than 1 with no proper divisors; two integers are coprime when their gcd is 1.

known.name: Logarithms and floor/ceiling
known.gloss: The base-2 logarithm and rounding down or up to integers, as used in size and depth bounds.

known.name: Vectors, matrices and inverses
known.gloss: Finite-dimensional vectors, matrices acting as linear maps, invertibility, and orthogonality via dot products.

known.name: Schoolbook and Karatsuba multiplication
known.gloss: Quadratic digit-by-digit multiplication and the divide-and-conquer improvement using three half-size products.

known.name: Divide-and-conquer recurrences
known.gloss: Solving cost recurrences such as T(n)=aT(n/b)+f(n) to obtain asymptotic bounds.

known.name: Limits, series and convergence
known.gloss: Limits of sequences, convergence of series such as geometric sums, used to bound errors and total costs.

known.name: Cartesian product and tuples
known.gloss: Ordered tuples of coordinates drawn from several index sets, used to index multidimensional arrays.

known.name: Permutations
known.gloss: A bijective rearrangement of positions in a list, composable and invertible.

known.name: Roots of unity
known.gloss: Complex numbers w with w^n=1, evenly spaced on the unit circle.

known.name: Rings and basic algebraic structures
known.gloss: Sets with addition and multiplication satisfying the standard laws, including integers modulo m and polynomials modulo a polynomial.

known.name: Fixed-point and rounding arithmetic
known.gloss: Representing reals by integers scaled by a power of 2, with bounded error from rounding or truncation.
